short: A highly agile French sesquiplane fighter that restored Allied air superiority in 1916.
full:
Entering service with the French Aéronautique Militaire in March 1916, the Nieuport 17 was a nimble sesquiplane fighter that rapidly became the mainstay of Allied aerial forces. Its design featured a standard upper wing and a much narrower lower wing, providing excellent downward visibility and a remarkable rate of climb. Armed with a synchronized Vickers machine gun or an over-wing Lewis gun, it possessed the speed and maneuverability required to decisively challenge the early German fighter squadrons.

The aircraft broke the dominance of the Fokker Eindecker and was instrumental in securing control of the skies over the Somme and Verdun. It was adopted by virtually every Allied nation and flown by leading aces, including Georges Guynemer, Albert Ball, and Billy Bishop. Though rendered obsolescent by heavier, faster fighters by mid-1917, the Nieuport 17 remained in secondary roles and trainer capacities well into the postwar era.
